name: Akshay Ruparelia
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Doorsteps.co.uk at age 17 and by age 19 the company was valued at £12 million, making him the UK's youngest millionaire.
early_history_summary: Ruparelia grew up in Harrow, London in a Gujarati Indian family where both parents are hearing impaired. He began selling sweets at age 12-13 and launched Doorsteps at 17 while studying for A-Levels, borrowing £7,000 from relatives. He hired call centers to handle client calls while he was at school, then returned calls in the evenings. The online estate agency disrupted the traditional property market with a £99 fixed-fee model.
family_context_summary: Born to Gujarati Indian parents in Hemel Hempstead; both parents are hearing impaired. Father Kaushik is a care worker, mother Renuka is a teaching assistant. Ruparelia served as a young carer, shouldering responsibility from an early age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents are a care worker and teaching assistant; no domain expertise in technology or real estate transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: young carer, deaf parents, grammar school, online estate agency disruption, £99 fee model
evidence_summary: Ruparelia grew up as a young carer to hearing-impaired parents, which instilled early responsibility and entrepreneurial drive. He attended Queen Elizabeth's School, Barnet, a selective grammar school. He launched Doorsteps at 17 with £7,000 borrowed from relatives, disrupting the UK property market with a low-cost online model. By 19, the company was valued at £12M and had become the UK's 18th largest estate agency. His parents' hearing impairment created adversity that catalyzed his independence and work ethic. He received an Oxford offer but deferred to focus on the business.
starting_point: Born in 1998 in Hemel Hempstead to Gujarati Indian parents who are both hearing impaired; father a care worker, mother a teaching assistant.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of brdge AI; previously founded Doorsteps.co.uk which sold over £1 billion worth of houses. Featured on Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe Technology 2021.

name: Markus Villig

By 2016, the company had expanded to multiple countries and he was featured as the youngest CEO on Forbes 30 Under 30 Baltics.
family_context_summary: Born in Tallinn, Estonia. His older brother Martin Villig is a serial tech entrepreneur who co-conceived the idea and co-founded the company. Family provided €5,000 loan for initial development.
